# Checks

[ci.yml](/.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs on every pull request and every push to `main`. Keep `ci.yml` and the checks it calls free of deploy steps and secrets, and keep their tokens read-only. [ci-checks.md](/docs/decisions/ci-checks.md) explains why.

## The checks

| Job in `ci.yml` | Workflow | Runs when a change touches | Also called by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `games` | `check-games.yml` | `games/`, except `games/platform/turn/` | `games.yml` |
| `turn` | `check-turn.yml` | `games/platform/turn/` | `games.yml` |
| `nginx` | `check-nginx.yml` | `infra/` | `infra.yml` |
| `project-names` | `check-project-names.yml` | `games/` or `temp-sites/projects/` | `games.yml` |
| `game-names` | `check-game-names.yml` | a `compose.yml` or `docker-compose.yml` anywhere, also with `.yaml`, or `infra/nginx/conf.d/games.conf` | none |
| `www` | `check-www.yml` | `www/` | none |
| `blog` | `check-blog.yml` | `blog/`, a [post](/blog/docs/posts.md) in `blog/src/posts/` included | none |
| `docs` | `check-docs.yml` | any file | none |

Every check also runs when `ci.yml`, its own workflow or the [deploy workflow](/.github/docs/deploys.md) that calls it changes. Only `games.yml` and `infra.yml` call their checks before every deploy, and a failing check stops the deploy. No other deploy workflow runs a check before it deploys. Markdown files start no check other than `docs`, apart from a post in `blog/src/posts/`, which also starts `blog`.

- `check-games.yml` tests the packages that the `games-changes` job finds, as [games-changes.md](/.github/docs/games-changes.md) says. When one of the workflows above or `games-changes.yml` changes, it tests every package. Its `test` job runs pnpm in the Node image of the Dockerfiles in `games/`, with pnpm from the image `ghcr.io/pnpm/pnpm` that they use, as [pnpm-in-images.md](/games/docs/decisions/pnpm-in-images.md) decides. The tag of the pnpm image is `<version>-alpine` with the version that `packageManager` in `games/package.json` names. Its `browser` job runs the browser tests of the same packages on the runner, in its Google Chrome, on the Node version of that image and with coturn in Docker, as [browser-tests.md](/games/docs/browser-tests.md) says. When they fail, it uploads their report and results as the `games-browser-tests` artifact. Its `images` job builds the image of each [deployment](/docs/glossary.md#deployment) with a `Dockerfile` that the `games-changes` job finds, or, in `ci.yml` when one of the workflows above or `games-changes.yml` changes, of every deployment of `games/` with a `Dockerfile`, from the context `games/` that `games.yml` gives `deploy-project.yml`, without a cache from earlier runs and without pushing it. Then it starts the image and waits up to 30 seconds for its health check to pass, and fails, with the container's log, when the check does not pass or the image has none, so a change that breaks the build or the start of an image fails before it reaches `main`. `games.yml` calls `check-games.yml` with every package and with the deployments that its `changes` job finds, so before each deploy it tests every package and builds and starts the images of the deployments that the push reaches. A new Node image changes `check-games.yml`, the Node version of its `browser` job and every Dockerfile in `games/` together. A new pnpm version changes `packageManager`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` and the tag of the pnpm image in `check-games.yml` and every Dockerfile in `games/` together.
- `check-nginx.yml` runs `nginx -t` on the nginx configs with throwaway self-signed certificates that it creates only for `nii.au` and `when.party`. A config that names another certificate file also needs that name in the loop of `check-nginx.yml` and in that of the tests' `proxy.sh`. Then it runs the smoke tests of the proxy, as [verification.md](/infra/docs/verification.md) says. [nginx-configs.md](/infra/docs/nginx-configs.md#checking-a-change) says how to run the same check locally.
- `check-game-names.yml` reads every `compose.yml` and `docker-compose.yml` that git tracks, also with `.yaml`, through `docker compose config`, so it reads list and mapping forms alike. It takes the names of the containers that nginx reaches for the games from the `server <name>:<port> resolve` lines of [games.conf](/infra/nginx/conf.d/games.conf). It fails when the container of `games/titles/<name>/compose.yml` is not `games-<name>` on `wp_games`, when a name from `games.conf` belongs to no container in `games/` on `wp_games`, or when another container's name, Compose service name or network alias starts with `games-` or is a name from `games.conf`. A service without `container_name` counts with Compose's default name, `<project>-<service>-1`. [game-names-check.md](/docs/decisions/game-names-check.md) explains why no deploy calls it.
- `check-www.yml` runs the browser tests of `www/` and, when they fail, uploads their report and screenshots as the `www-tests` artifact and the new screenshots as `www-snapshots`, as [tests.md](/www/docs/tests.md) says.
- `check-blog.yml` builds the image of `blog/` as [site.yml](/.github/workflows/site.yml) does, without pushing it, so a change or a post that breaks the build fails before it reaches `main`.
- `check-docs.yml` runs [check-docs.py](/.github/scripts/check-docs.py) on every [document](/docs/glossary.md#document), apart from its fenced code blocks and code spans, and on the test files of the [specifications](/docs/conventions/specs.md). It reads inline links whose targets have no spaces or parentheses, and not reference definitions such as `[x]: path`. A test file is a `.ts`, `.js` or `.sh` file whose name starts with a number and a hyphen, such as `1-match.test.ts`, in or below a `tests` folder. The requirements of a specification file are its top-level list items that start with a [requirement ID](/docs/conventions/specs.md#content), in backticks or not. The script reads an `it` or `test` call whose name is a quoted string or a template literal, with no modifier or with `only`, `concurrent`, `sequential`, `skip`, `fixme`, `fail`, `fails` or `todo`; a call with one of the last five does not run. It does not read other forms, such as `it.each` or a name held in a variable. The IDs at the start of a name or argument are separated by spaces or commas, and each ends at a character other than a letter, digit, underscore or hyphen, such as the colon in "2-3: shows the board". The script fails when:
  - a link without a scheme such as `https:` leads to no file or folder of the repository, or to no heading of a Markdown file, with the anchors that GitHub gives headings;
  - a requirement ID that is the text of a link to a specification file, or that stands in backticks before "of" or "in", up to three words and such a link, as the [writing rules](/docs/conventions/writing.md) write it, is not a requirement of that file;
  - a requirement of a specification file has the number of another file;
  - a requirement has no test: no test file named after its specification file, as the [testing rules](/docs/conventions/tests.md) name it, has its ID among the IDs at the start of the name of a call that runs, among the IDs at the start of the first argument of a command in a `.sh` file, or in an array of quoted IDs, such as a table cell;
  - the IDs at the start of such a name or argument, or an ID in such an array, include one that is not a requirement of that specification file;
  - in a `.ts` or `.js` test file, the name of a call that the script reads starts with no requirement ID, unless it starts with `${` and an expression with `ids`, such as `${cell.ids.join(' ')}`, which takes its IDs from table cells;
  - in a `.sh` test file, the first argument of a command starts with no requirement ID while the first argument of the same command elsewhere in the file does;
  - a test file is named after no specification file of the innermost [project](/docs/glossary.md#project) or [module](/docs/glossary.md#module) with a specification that holds it.

  The script prints each error as a line `path:line: message` and as an annotation. Run in the root of a working tree, it gives the same errors and also reads the files that git does not track yet. [docs-check.md](/docs/decisions/docs-check.md) explains why it runs in CI on every change.

## Skipping and the result job

`ci.yml` has no `paths`. Its `changes` job finds what changed, and its `games-changes` job finds the affected packages of `games/`. Every check other than `docs` has an `if:` on their outputs; `docs` runs for every change. A workflow that `paths` keeps from running leaves a required status check pending, while a job skipped by `if:` counts as passed.

The `result` job fails when any job it needs failed or was cancelled. So the ruleset `main-pull-requests` requires only `result`, as [github-setup.md](/.github/docs/github-setup.md#main-branch) says.

## Adding a check

A new check that runs only for some changes gets an output in the `changes` job. That output is also true when `ci.yml`, the check's own workflow or the deploy workflow that calls it changes. The check's job goes into the `needs` of `result`.
